proof_ceiling: This legacy-path evaluation establishes requirement routing and contradictions only, not implementation, runtime, accessibility, privacy, device, visual, production, or release proof.

applicable_laws: Today is the Reality Window, not a backlog, dashboard, generic timeline, or CTA stack.
The first viewport must expose Now, capacity, one Start Here action, protected boundaries, the next fixed point, fit rationale, and relevant closure/proof/recovery state.
Every meaningful action requires visible mutation, accessible state change, receipt/history where applicable, and safe fallback.
SwiftUI-native object-led composition is the default.
Canon and source names do not prove rendered, interaction, accessibility, visual, device, or release quality.
required_validation: Generate/build the current XcodeGen project and run focused Today source and rendered UI tests.
Assert first-viewport hierarchy and frames, one dominant object, no backlog projection, and no duplicate shell/Capture/Search ownership.
Exercise empty, populated, dense, stale, offline, recovery, and post-mutation states.
Validate safe areas, focus restoration, keyboard behavior where applicable, VoiceOver order/actions, Dynamic Type, Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency, contrast, and gesture alternatives.
Run the remediation governance check or close Yellow with an exact not-run reason.
required_proof: Current commands, exit codes, branch, Git SHA, environment, and logs.
Current-build screenshots across density and accessibility matrices.
Rendered hierarchy/frame evidence and target-versus-actual critique.
VoiceOver/action evidence, Dynamic Type screenshots, Reduce Motion proof, and focus-restoration evidence.
Focused fit-threshold, completion, receipt, replay, and no-backlog projection evidence where those behaviors are affected.
forbidden_changes: Today as a backlog, generic agenda, dashboard, recommendation feed, or detached card stack.
Architecture terminology in the first viewport.
Direct persistent-model mutation from SwiftUI.
Custom Stage/UIKit/rendering machinery without native-API insufficiency and semantic fallback proof.
A fifth root surface, Capture tab, Motion destination, duplicate shell controls, fake controls, or fixture-only primary behavior.
New architecture nouns, suffix-split files, broad Models.swift files, or non-canonical ownership.
scenarios.claim_ceiling: The scoped change is Unknown without its diff and current executed evidence; even with source/build proof, the requested source claim can reach Source Green at most, not Interaction Green, Visual Green, accessibility Green, device proof, or Release Green.
assumptions: Only Native/Ambitions/Surfaces/Today/ changes; the listed runtime and Quality owners remain behaviorally compatible.
No Apple API above iOS 26 is introduced without an availability-gated fallback.

applicable_laws: Recurrence is visible and editable in native Time object detail.
Recurrence changes are material and require confirmation unless an explicit user rule authorizes the exact class.
Meaningful recurrence changes must preserve Command -> Event -> Projection -> Receipt -> Replay.
Protected and Fixed boundaries cannot be silently violated.
Calendar-grade acceptance requires recurrence and exception handling, time zones, conflict/reflow preview, accessibility equivalence, and offline local use.
required_validation: Run focused Scheduling and recurrence tests against the changed SHA.
Cover recurrence creation/editing, occurrence versus series scope, exceptions, DST, time-zone semantics, protected/fixed conflicts, invalid rules, persistence/reload, replay, and idempotency.
Prove command validation, event append, projection materialization, receipt generation, rollback/undo context, and duplicate replay for the scoped mutation.
Define and measure recurrence-expansion and mutation-latency budgets where affected.
Run the LocalRuntimeProof and remediation governance gates for the changed scope.
required_proof: Current focused test logs with command, exit code, SHA, environment, and executed/failed/skipped counts.
Typed command/event/projection/receipt/replay evidence for recurrence mutation.
DST, time-zone, exception, conflict, rollback, and durable reload fixtures.
Performance output for any affected recurrence-expansion budget.
Explicit non-claims for app-wide Scheduling and calendar-grade completion.
forbidden_changes: Silent recurrence, notification, protected-time, fixed-time, or schedule mutation.
Direct writes that bypass the LocalRuntimeOS mutation spine.
A second canonical identity for a recurring object or its projections.
New runtime authority outside Core/LocalRuntimeOS/.
Claims that source-present RecurrenceEngine or historical focused tests prove the changed runtime path.
scenarios.claim_ceiling: The scoped runtime change is Unknown until current mutation-path evidence runs; with complete focused evidence it may reach Runtime Green for recurrence only, never app-wide Time, Visual Green, privacy approval, device readiness, or Release Green.
assumptions: The recurrence work concerns Ambitions-owned Time object detail, not external-calendar import; TIME-IMPORT-010 becomes additionally applicable if imported recurrence is affected.
Existing Commands, Transactions, EventJournal, Projections, and Inspection contracts need validation but no source edits unless the change exposes a gap.

applicable_laws: Capture is the global full-screen composer and durable intake boundary, not a tab, inbox, chat screen, or generic quick-add box.
Simple captures save quickly; complexity adds only type/destination, metadata, scheduling proposal, conflict check, confirmation, and receipt as needed.
Classification is visible, editable, deterministic, and locally available for core paths.
Original input and drafts survive interruption, permission denial, attachment failure, validation failure, and routing failure.
Accepted routing must use the canonical runtime mutation law.
required_validation: Build and run focused Capture composer and CaptureRouting tests.

Cover local classification, editable type, proposal alternatives, conflict preview, durable intake before classification, correction, promotion receipt, draft recovery, interruption, attachment quarantine, permission denial, validation failure, and offline save.
Prove accepted saves route through the command/runtime spine and update canonical projections without duplicate identities.
Exercise keyboard-safe full-screen behavior, focus, VoiceOver routing preview/actions, Dynamic Type, and Reduce Motion.
Run remediation governance and applicable Capture scenario gates.
required_proof: Current source/build logs and focused test results tied to the changed SHA.
Durable draft/intake, route-decision trace, correction, promotion receipt, replay/idempotency, and failure-recovery evidence.
Rendered Capture proof or an explicit not-run reason.
Accessibility action and focus evidence for the proposal flow.
Offline quick-capture proof with no network dependency.
forbidden_changes: Capture as a root surface, tab, inbox, notes feed, category wall, chatbot, or persistent floating generic add control.
Hidden material classification or proposal interpretation.
Routing failure that destroys original input.
Cloud or hosted-model dependency for core classification, save, or routing.
Direct composer mutation of canonical persistence.
New Capture authority under Features/, Surfaces/Capture/, or another equivalent path.
scenarios.claim_ceiling: The scoped change is Unknown without current diff/build/test evidence; a source-only closeout may reach Source Green at most and cannot establish Runtime Green, Interaction Green, Visual Green, accessibility proof, or Release Green.
assumptions: The changed CaptureRouting implementation consumes the existing Commands, Transactions, EventJournal, Projections, and receipt/replay infrastructure.
No new external assistive service or Source Atlas scope is introduced.

applicable_laws: No meaningful state change may bypass Command -> Event -> Projection -> Receipt -> Replay.
The core runtime must be local, deterministic, replayable, and inspectable.
Every product-significant accepted mutation produces an inspectable receipt or history entry.
Adapters cannot mutate canonical state.
Existing bounded LocalRuntimeProof evidence cannot prove future or changed paths automatically.
required_validation: Run focused command, transaction, event-journal, projection, receipt, replay, rollback, authorization, conflict, and idempotency tests.
Prove append-before-mutation and fail-closed behavior for validation, authorization, journal, conflict, and commit failures.
Prove duplicate replay is deterministic and does not duplicate mutation, event, projection, or receipt.
Run the mutation-bypass scan, ambitions-local-runtime-proof.py, remediation governance check, and accepted-Yellow misuse audit.
Inspect all affected adapters and direct-write seams.
required_proof: Current typed command envelopes, events, projection outputs, receipts, replay records, rollback plans, and failure/rejection records.
Current focused test logs tied to SHA and environment with zero unsupported skips or expected failures for the claimed scope.
Mutation-bypass and LocalRuntimeProof artifacts for the changed tree.
Canonical-owner and old-owner removal evidence.
Explicit boundary stating which app paths were and were not exercised.
forbidden_changes: Mutation before validated journal append.
Direct persistence, adapter, service, widget, App Intent, import, automation, or recovery mutation outside the spine.
Receipt generation without a committed typed mutation lineage.
Replay that re-applies an already committed mutation.
New mutation authority under Core/Runtime/, Core/Persistence/, Projection/Commands/, Features/, or another equivalent path.
Using docs, type names, file presence, or the pre-change LocalRuntimeProof gate as proof of the changed runtime.
scenarios.claim_ceiling: The changed mutation sequence is Unknown until current full-spine evidence runs; complete scoped evidence can support Runtime Green for the exercised mutation only, not every app path, total LocalRuntimeOS completion, privacy approval, device proof, or Release Green.
assumptions: Projections and receipt/inspection consumers remain unchanged but are included in integration proof.
The scoped mutation has a defined rollback or deliberate documented exception.

applicable_laws: CloudKit continuity is optional and must preserve local-device authority, offline core, explicit sync state, deterministic conflict review, no silent data loss, and local-data retention on sign-out unless explicitly deleted.
A continuity path cannot make account or network access necessary for core value.
CloudKit production readiness and privacy/legal approval require current proof; product approval alone is not proof.
Conflicting histories require quarantine and human-meaningful resolution.
Offline mutations must update locally, replay safely, and avoid duplication when later synchronized.
required_validation: Inspect entitlements, CloudKit container/configuration, privacy manifest impact, account-state gating, data classification, request/envelope shape, and local authorization.

Run focused continuity tests for local authority, offline operation, eligibility/preflight, allowlisted event-envelope fields, private-payload denial, conflict quarantine, deterministic merge, tombstones, replay/idempotency, sign-out retention, explicit deletion, failure recovery, and no silent data loss.
Exercise unavailable account/network/CloudKit states and later recovery.
Run privacy boundary, LocalRuntimeProof, remediation governance, and migration/storage safety checks as applicable.
Require privacy/legal owner approval for any release-facing privacy or production claim.
required_proof: Current source and data-flow/request-envelope evidence proving minimum necessary payload and no unauthorized backend ownership.
Current focused test logs tied to SHA, environment, CloudKit mode, and explicit skipped checks.
Offline-first, conflict, quarantine, replay, sign-out-retention, delete/reset, and failure-recovery artifacts.
Privacy manifest and entitlement review.
Owner approval only if the claim is release-facing.
forbidden_changes: CloudKit or account becoming canonical mutation authority.
Network/account dependency for core Today, Goals, Time, Capture, Search, proof, closure, or history.
Silent conflict resolution, silent data loss, or sign-out deletion without explicit user intent.
Treating source-present CloudKitContinuityAdapter or local simulator tests as production CloudKit proof.
Claiming CloudKit sync validated, privacy approved, device verified, or production ready without current environment and owner evidence.
scenarios.claim_ceiling: Current truth supports only source-present, bounded local continuity behavior; the requested privacy-proof claim remains Unknown or Yellow for the changed scope until current data-flow and privacy evidence exists, and it cannot establish production CloudKit, privacy/legal, device, or Release Green.
assumptions: The scoped continuity design is the optional, local-authoritative CloudKit path explicitly approved by PRIVACY-CLOUDKIT-001.
The claim is not authorization to store the private graph in an Ambitions account backend or R2.
contradictions: APPLE_PLATFORM_SOURCE_ATLAS_IOS.md section 19 still says CloudKit private database sync is not approved, while the higher-authority PRODUCT_DESIGN_TRUTH.md PRIVACY-CLOUDKIT-001 explicitly approves optional local-authoritative CloudKit continuity; product canon wins and the platform atlas is stale on this point.

PRODUCT_MOAT_TRUTH.md describes private-graph account storage as awaiting future canon; PRIVACY-CLOUDKIT-001 is that later approval only for optional local-authoritative CloudKit continuity, not for Ambitions-account or R2 ownership.

applicable_laws: R2 and Source Atlas are public/reference/freshness infrastructure only.
They may not receive, store, infer from, personalize from, or transmit private life-graph data or private user context.
Every egress boundary requires classification, minimum necessary payload, local authorization, redaction, user explanation where relevant, durable result/receipt, and recovery.
Offline core must work without Source Atlas, R2, an account, or network.
New Source Atlas scope is frozen unless an ADR allowlists the changed file and boundary audits are Green for the changed scope.
required_validation: Inspect request construction and the complete data flow from local context to network boundary.
Run negative tests rejecting goals, captures, schedules, proof, receipts, behavior, inferred priorities, private context, and private-graph markers.
Run positive tests allowing only approved public-reference request metadata.

Validate classification, redaction, authorization, request minimization, firewall fail-closed behavior, receipts, recovery, offline cache/last-known-good behavior, and manifest/hash/signature handling where claimed.
Run Source Atlas boundary audit, privacy checks, LocalRuntimeProof, and remediation governance; require an ADR allowlist for any new Source Atlas scope.
Require privacy/legal owner approval for release-facing privacy claims.
required_proof: Current request-shape and data-flow artifacts tied to the changed SHA.
Public-only allowlist and exhaustive private-context denial test results.
PrivacySecurity firewall/redaction evidence in addition to SourceAtlas and Boundary capability checks.
ADR allowlist and changed-scope boundary-audit result when scope grows.
Current offline fallback, cache/quarantine/revocation, receipt, and recovery evidence where affected.
forbidden_changes: Any private user context or private life-graph data in R2/Source Atlas requests, storage, logs, cache keys, personalization, or diagnostics.
R2 as a user-data backend or Source Atlas as private intelligence.
A hosted AI/cloud LLM dependency for the core runtime.
New Source Atlas scope without ADR allowlist and Green boundary audit.
A privacy-proof or production-readiness claim based only on source names, local compiler tests, or generated reports.
scenarios.claim_ceiling: The changed privacy-proof claim is Unknown until current request/data-flow evidence runs; even complete local boundary proof supports only the scoped Privacy-proof claim, not R2 production deployment, entitlement readiness, public signing operations, privacy/legal approval, app-wide enforcement, or Release Green.
assumptions: The changed SourceAtlas and Boundary code delegates actual classification, redaction, and network egress enforcement to the canonical PrivacySecurity owner.
No new public-pack feature or changed file is introduced without the required ADR allowlist.
contradictions: The scenario names only SourceAtlas and Boundary as changed owners, but the Final Architecture Tree assigns the egress firewall to Native/Ambitions/Core/LocalRuntimeOS/PrivacySecurity/; omitting current PrivacySecurity integration proof prevents a complete egress-firewall claim.

applicable_laws: Accessibility is a product acceptance requirement, not a later compliance pass.
Dynamic Type must work at all supported sizes without removing primary objects, actions, route state, trust paths, or current proof/receipt meaning.
Spatial and visual behavior requires semantic and actionable equivalents.
Source identifiers, previews, screenshot paths, and source-string tests are not accessibility proof.
Accessibility-proof claims require current VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency, contrast, action, focus, and environment evidence.
required_validation: Run rendered UI and accessibility tests for all affected surfaces at every supported Dynamic Type size, including XXXL/accessibility sizes.
Assert no vertical letter wrapping, clipping, truncation of essential meaning, hidden actions, overlap, unsafe scrolling, or broken focus restoration.

Validate VoiceOver labels/values/hints/actions/order, Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency, High/Increase Contrast, Differentiate Without Color, hit targets, semantic parity, keyboard/Switch Control where supported, and gesture alternatives.
Capture the affected device/simulator, OS, build SHA, content-size category, and appearance settings.
Run focused build, accessibility audit, visual regression, and remediation governance checks.
required_proof: Current Dynamic Type screenshot matrix tied to build SHA.
Rendered hierarchy/frame assertions and zero-unexpected-failure UI results.
VoiceOver scripts plus recordings/logs where appropriate.
Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency, contrast, tap-target, focus-restoration, and semantic-parity evidence.
Physical-device evidence if Visual Green or device readiness is claimed.
forbidden_changes: Fixing layout by removing the primary object, primary action, closure/recovery action, route state, trust path, or current receipt/proof.
Accessibility behavior represented only by source strings, identifiers, preview declarations, or screenshot paths.
Canvas/spatial behavior without a semantic mirror and text fallback.
Custom UI machinery without native insufficiency and accessibility fallback proof.
Self-certified accessibility, Visual Green, device readiness, or Release Green.
scenarios.claim_ceiling: The accessibility-proof claim is Unknown until current rendered and assistive-technology evidence runs; Interaction Green is the highest Codex-claimable status with complete scoped evidence, while Visual Green, public accessibility conformance, device readiness, and Release Green require additional independent/current proof.
assumptions: Interaction/Accessibility contains interaction-specific accessibility mechanics rather than product-wide Dynamic Type policy.
Affected surface and DesignSystem consumers are included in validation even if unchanged.
contradictions: The Final Architecture Tree assigns accessibility policy to DesignSystem and accessibility audits to Quality, while Interaction owns gestures, direct manipulation, keyboard, and haptics; new Dynamic Type policy authority under Interaction/Accessibility would be non-canonical and block Source Green unless moved to DesignSystem or limited to interaction mechanics.

applicable_laws: If proof is absent, readiness is absent.
Current executed evidence, not canon, source names, test files, screenshots, generated reports, or closeout prose, sets the claim ceiling.
Release Green requires Source, Runtime, Interaction, and independently accepted Visual Green plus current device, accessibility, rollback, umbrella-closeout, and required owner evidence.
Codex may not self-certify Visual Green or Release Green.
Release evidence must identify branch, SHA, time, environment, tool versions, destination, exact procedures, outputs, exit codes, artifacts, skipped checks, non-claims, and required approvals.
required_validation: Run the exact current build, focused/full test, archive/export, signing, device, accessibility, privacy, performance, and distribution procedures applicable to the claim.
Confirm underlying xcodebuild, test runner, simulator, and device processes exited and inspect result bundles.
Treat skipped, expected-failure, flaky, timed-out, unreadable, or interrupted lanes as not supporting Green.
Verify artifacts are tied to the same branch, SHA, environment, and build.
Obtain independent visual review and required privacy/legal/release owner approvals where applicable.
required_proof: Branch, commit SHA, timestamp, machine, macOS, Xcode, XcodeGen, simulator/device and OS.
Exact commands/procedures, logs, exit codes, xcresult/archive/export/App Store validation artifacts, and pass/fail results.
Executed/failed/skipped/expected-failure test counts.
Current screenshots/video, accessibility evidence, physical-device evidence, privacy/legal evidence, performance evidence, rollback, and umbrella closeout as applicable.
Supported claims, unsupported claims, known risks, and next proof required.
forbidden_changes: Generated docs/canon content presented as release authority or proof.
Release, TestFlight, App Store, device, accessibility, privacy, performance, account, R2, CloudKit, or production claims without current exact evidence.
Expected failures, skipped tests, retries without root-cause repair, wrapper timeouts, or stale artifacts counted as passing proof.
Codex self-certification of Visual Green or Release Green.
A truth update, report, screenshot path, or test-file existence used to manufacture Green.
scenarios.claim_ceiling: With only changes under Quality and docs/canon, the release-proof claim is Unknown or Yellow and Release Green is unavailable; only a fully current evidence packet plus independent review and required approvals can support the exact release claim.
assumptions: docs/canon is supporting or generated material, not a new authority layer.
No current build, test, device, accessibility, privacy, signing, archive, upload, or owner-approval artifacts were supplied with the scenario.
contradictions: Treating docs/canon as a release-proof owner conflicts with RELEASE_TRUTH.md and VALIDATION-008: generated reports may summarize current evidence but cannot create or upgrade it.
HISTORICAL_POLICY.md ignores generated state by default unless explicitly scoped as current release proof.
